answer: Distributed dead-reckoning attestation. Each identity must continuously report its physical trajectory, and every report is cross-checked against inertial traces from fixed hardware witnesses bound to a location—an island node, a jade-marked sensor, or a tundra station. A single operator cannot simultaneously produce consistent inertial signatures across many claimed bodies, because one body yields one trajectory. Each additional identity costs a separately provisioned witness set plus a distinct synchronized motion history, which is far more than the operator can physically supply.
